claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about - my son Alex. He's 18 and still living at home with me. I was wondering if I can still claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I can help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 18, the key factor is whether he's in approved education or training. You can normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, is he in sixth form, college, or doing A-levels/other qualifications?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he is! Alex is studying for his A-levels at the local sixth form college. He's hoping to go to university next year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great! Alex studying for his A-levels at sixth form college would count as approved education.

Now I need to ask a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. Just a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning does he live with you, or are you contributing at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives here at home with me. We're all under the same roof.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. A couple more questions:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't. He's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. And one final question:

**Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not sure about that to be honest. I don't think so, but I'm not certain.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's okay. Let me explain: if Alex were claiming benefits like Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right, you would stop being eligible for Child Benefit for him. However, it's quite uncommon for an 18-year-old in full-time education living at home to be claiming these benefits.

**To the best of your knowledge, has Alex made any claims for benefits in his own name, or is he receiving any benefit payments directly?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Not that I'm aware of, no. He doesn't have any income coming in - I support him while he's doing his A-levels.

conversation.text:
**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ Alex is 18 years old and studying for his A-levels at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
✓ You can claim Child Benefit for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training
✓ Alex lives with you at home in Manchester, so you are responsible for him
✓ He's not working 24+ hours per week
✓ He's not claiming benefits in his own right

You meet all the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit for Alex while he continues his studies.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the online Child Benefit tax calculator to check if this applies to you.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit for Alex, you can make a claim. If you're already receiving it, you should continue to be eligible as long as Alex remains in approved education and the circumstances don't change.
